name: A Lighthouse called Kanata
about_text: A Lighthouse called Kanata is a contemporary art gallery in the Jingumae area of Shibuya-ku, Tokyo, near Omotesando Station. It was established in 2007 by Wahei Aoyama with the aim of introducing contemporary Japanese art and aesthetics to an international audience. The gallery's program centers on sculpture and painting by artists working within an emerging strand of Japanese aesthetics that reinstates beauty, technique, and materiality as central concerns, spanning media such as ceramics, glass, lacquer, metal, bamboo and wood alongside painting. The gallery frames its mission around a 'Return to Innocence' in contemporary art practice, positioning its roster of artists, many working in traditional craft mediums, within a global contemporary art context.
hours_text: 11am to 6pm on Tuesdays to Saturdays, and by Appointment. Closed Sundays, Mondays and National Holidays.

notes: Gallery was previously known as 'Yufuku' before becoming A Lighthouse called Kanata (per 2020/06/17 news item). A 2025/06/03 news item states the gallery 'will be relocating to Omotesando,' but no new address distinct from the current Jingumae address was found in the supplied pages, so only one current location is listed.

triage.site_notes: Site is organised with distinct sections for artists (roster with dozens of individual artist pages under /artists), works (product-style catalogue under /works, not separately labeled), exhibitions (a filterable archive covering years 2014-2026 split by category all/art-fairs/exhibitions-projects and time upcoming/past, doubling as both current and archive), and news (paginated by year and category, plus individual press/closure announcements); English mirror exists under /en. No dedicated fairs page beyond exhibitions filtered by art-fairs category, which is already captured as exhibitions_archive/current.
